At the top-right cell, every value to its left is no larger, while every value below is no smaller. If this corner is above target, its entire remaining column is too large, so move left. If it is below target, its entire remaining row is too small, so move down. Equality finishes the search immediately.

The unsearched candidates always form a rectangle below and to the left of the current corner. Each comparison removes a whole side without removing any possible target. Row and column indices only move in one direction, bounding the search by their combined lengths.
This approach also handles repeated values: the eliminated side inequalities are sufficient even when neighboring values are equal.
